decisions.headline: An Android checkout break in Barcelona and Milan since 14 Oct is costing about €700k a month in revenue; together with a Madrid Home edition that sold out on day 3 (about €300k a month) and late deliveries in London (about €125–197k a month), it explains most of the 6% revenue fall. These need fixing before any budget changes.

findings.title: Android checkout broken in Barcelona and Milan since 14 Oct
findings.evidence: Android checkout-to-order from 14 Oct to 1 Nov: Barcelona 22.2% (2,161 orders from 9,725 checkouts) vs 62.7% before (9,166/14,611); Milan 22.0% (1,900/8,627) vs 62.6% (7,600/12,149). Peers 61.9–62.1%. iOS and desktop are normal. Payment complaints: Milan 9.7%, Barcelona 8.3%, vs 2.5% elsewhere. Lost revenue ≈ €234k (Barcelona) + €206k (Milan) over 19 days ≈ €700k a month. The last 7 days are still at 22.7%.

findings.title: Madrid Home Edition 11 was stocked at 270 units, not 8,334, and sold out on 21 Oct; ads kept running
findings.evidence: MAD-HOM-E10 capacity was 270 vs 8,334 for earlier editions. The edition runs until 29 Nov. Madrid Home revenue/day fell from €21.9k (14 days) to €11.6k (11 days), and sessions/day from 9,388 to 4,995. That is about €300k a month in lost revenue. Spend in the last 7 days was still €18.0k.

findings.title: London deliveries arriving a week late, which is hurting repeat purchases
findings.evidence: Late-delivery comments are 32% of all comments (70 of 219) vs 5.4% elsewhere, and 34% in the last 14 days. NPS fell from -7 to -35. Weekly email orders fell from about 1,300 to about 820 and SMS orders from about 450 to about 290, starting in the same week the complaints rose (week 40). Repeat share is 8.9% vs 12.7% for peers. Revenue at stake is €125k–197k a month.

findings.title: Budget is stuck in saturated channels: google_brand and meta_retargeting
findings.evidence: Model marginal ROAS: google_brand 0.00–0.84 and meta_retargeting often below 1, vs tiktok, youtube and creators at 3–7. meta_retargeting's platform-claimed ROAS is 3.49 vs 1.64 first-party. 21 of 44 market-lines have R² ≥0.80. The plan at the tool's default cap shows €136.8k/week of extra revenue across the 19 lines that could be read.

findings.title: São Paulo Home gets the least revenue per search of the established Home markets but has the best marginal return
findings.evidence: Revenue per search over 8 weeks is 1.39, vs 1.43–1.75 for peers. Marginal ROAS 3.81 (R² 0.988). Lisbon Beauty's marginal ROAS is 0.82, and Lisbon's MER is 4.82 vs a peer range of 5.44–6.33.

findings.title: Rain clearly lifts Home sales
findings.evidence: Rain effect on Home orders: Paris +31.3% [28.6, 34.1], London +31.5% [28.9, 34.2], São Paulo +15.1% [9.9, 20.5]; 300–434 days of data per market. Fashion drops falls in rain, so it stays out of any rain rule.

findings.title: Seasonal, not problems: New York's dip and lower Fashion drops
findings.evidence: New York revenue/day is €96.3k vs €99.0k last year, with revenue per search flat. Fashion drops searches are falling seasonally.

findings.title: Rain clearly lifts Home sales

input.summary: The two biggest problems are an Android checkout break in Barcelona and Milan since 14 Oct, worth about €700k/month in lost revenue together, and a Madrid Home stockout since 21 Oct, worth about €310k/month, with ads still running. Smaller items: London's email and SMS revenue has fallen, Lisbon spent more for no extra revenue, and Mexico City is far behind earlier launches. The New York revenue drop and the Fashion drops dip are seasonal.

findings.title: Android checkout-to-order fell from about 62% to about 22% starting 14 Oct
findings.line: all lines (Home, Fashion drops, Beauty, Gifts all fell 62→54% overall)
findings.evidence: Android checkout-to-order went from 65.5% (550 checkouts) on 13 Oct to 21.5% (502 checkouts) on 14 Oct. It has stayed at 20–23% every day since. Weeks 3–4: 1,592 orders from 7,136 checkouts, against 62.8% in the prior 4 weeks (9,094 orders from 14,480 checkouts). Peer Android rate is 61.91–62.11% (last year 62.01%). iOS (62.9%) and desktop (60.6%) are unchanged, and order value is flat at €59.5. All of Barcelona's 28-day checkout-to-order is 54.0%, against a peer range of 61.96–61.97%. No significance test was run; the gap is about 40 points on roughly 3,500 checkouts a week.

findings.title: Same Android checkout break, starting the same day (14 Oct)
findings.evidence: Android checkout-to-order went from 58.4% (385 checkouts) on 13 Oct to 20.1% (442 checkouts) on 14 Oct. Weeks 3–4: 1,417 orders from 6,399 checkouts (about 22%), against 62.5% before (7,670 from 12,280). Peer range is 61.91–62.11%. iOS and desktop are normal at 61.6% and 63.1%. This one break explains all of Milan's other outliers: revenue/day €44.3k against a peer range of €52.5–56.0k (last year €51.4k), MER 5.44 against 6.33–6.66, and CPA €25.15 against €19.81–21.41.

findings.title: Home Edition 11 sold out on day 3 because it was stocked at 270 units instead of 8,334; ads kept running
findings.evidence: MAD-HOM-E10 (Edition 11) went on sale 19 Oct with capacity 270. Every other Madrid Home edition has 8,334, and it is the only product under 2,000 units. It was marked sold out on 21 Oct. Daily Home revenue fell from an average of €21.9k (12–21 Oct) to €11.6k (22 Oct–1 Nov), and sessions halved (about 9,400 to about 4,800 a day). Ad spend over those 11 sold-out days was still €29,057. Over 28 days, Madrid Home revenue was €497.9k against €562.4k before, and ROAS fell from 8.46 to 6.75.

findings.title: London's email and SMS revenue fell about 31%, which pulled repeat share below peers
findings.evidence: Repeat share is 8.87%, against 12.17% in the prior period, 12.77% last year and a peer range of 12.66–12.69%. Email sessions were about 21k a week until mid-September, then 17.3k in the week of 28 Sep and about 13–14k a week since. Email orders went from about 1,290 to about 830 a week, and SMS orders from about 450 to about 290 a week. Combined email and SMS revenue was €266.9k over 28 days, against €388.6k before. Other London channels are flat.

findings.title: Lisbon spent about 10% more with no extra revenue: MER and organic share are below peers
findings.line: all lines (spend rose on Beauty, Gifts and Home)
findings.evidence: MER is 4.82, against 5.58 in the prior period, 5.64 last year and a peer range of 5.44–6.33. Ad spend was €198.0k, against €179.7k in the prior period, while revenue was €953.8k against €1,002.5k. Paid share is 50.9% against a peer range of 43.8–44.1%; organic share is 37.2% against 44.34–44.35%. Revenue per search is in line with peers (Gifts 1.51, Home 1.52), so demand capture is fine and the problem is the extra spend.

findings.title: Mexico City launch is far behind earlier launches at the same age
findings.evidence: The market launched 6 Sep and is 8 weeks old. The benchmark tool puts revenue/day now at €2,535, against Miami at €36,690 and São Paulo at €50,190 at the same age (6% of their median). CPA is €38.87 against a peer range of €17.49–19.44 (down from €56.74). Revenue per search is 0.44 for Beauty, 0.64 for Fashion drops, 0.75 for Gifts and 0.82 for Home, against peers at about 0.75–1.5. Caveat: the same tool reports 28-day revenue/day as €10.4k, so the launch figure needs checking.

findings.title: Beauty captures much less of its search demand than peers, but this is long-standing
findings.evidence: Revenue per search is 0.62 (788,676 searches over 28 days), against about 0.72–0.86 in other Beauty markets (median about 0.79). It was 0.61 in the same period last year. Madrid's search volume is higher than Paris's with about half the population, so the search index may be inflated. Revenue/day is €17.6k, the same as last year (€17.7k) and above peers (€9.8–10.5k). The euro figure is the upper bound if Madrid reached the peer capture rate.

proposed_actions.action: Escalate to engineering today: Android checkout/payment in Barcelona and Milan since 14 Oct. Check the release or payment-provider change made that day.
proposed_actions.why: It is the same day and the same device in both markets, and iOS and desktop are normal there. It costs about €700k/month in revenue together.

proposed_actions.action: Fix Madrid Home Edition 11 capacity (270 → the usual 8,334) and restock, or pull the next edition forward. Pause or redirect Madrid Home ads until stock is back.
proposed_actions.why: Revenue has halved since 22 Oct, and €29k of ads ran while the product was sold out.

proposed_actions.action: Check London email/SMS sending: volume, list, deliverability and any changes since late September.
proposed_actions.why: Sessions from both channels fell about 35% from the week of 28 Sep while every other London channel stayed flat, which explains the repeat-share drop.

proposed_actions.action: Take Lisbon spend back to the previous level (about €180k per 4 weeks).
proposed_actions.why: The extra €18k produced no extra revenue, and MER is now below peers and last year.

proposed_actions.action: Confirm Mexico City's launch revenue figures, then review CAC and the channel mix before scaling.
proposed_actions.why: It is at 6% of earlier launches at the same age, and CPA is double that of peers.

not_problems: New York revenue/day fell 24% against the prior 4 weeks (€96.3k vs €126.4k), but it matches last year (€99.0k). Search interest fell about 20% over the same time and revenue per search is flat (e.g. Home 1.40 vs 1.45). CPA is €21.54, against €22.28 last year. This is seasonal.
Fashion drops revenue fell 10–15% in almost every market (e.g. London -14%, Berlin -13%) as searches also fell. This follows the drop/season calendar, not a problem in any one market.
Milan's revenue, MER and CPA outliers are all caused by the Android checkout break, not by marketing.
iOS and desktop checkout-to-order are within the normal range in every market (the scans flagged nothing).
Madrid Beauty revenue is normal against last year and above peers; only its demand-capture ratio is low, and it was just as low last year.
Gross profit was not computed because margin data (unit_costs) was not queried. All euro figures are revenue.

input.summary: Rain clearly lifts Home sales in all 12 measured markets (+12% to +33%, every 95% range above zero). Paris, São Paulo and London Home are the best places for a rain rule over the next 14 days, worth about €40k, €40k and €26k of forecast uplift; Fashion drops reliably loses sales in rain. The biggest uncaptured demand is Madrid Beauty (75% of potential, about €353k over 8 weeks). It is a long-standing reach gap, not a new failure, and November's seasonal and holiday demand (gift searches ramp, US Thanksgiving, French/US holiday on 11 Nov) argues for moving spend toward Gifts and Home, not Fashion drops.

findings.title: Home: strong, significant rain effect everywhere – the main candidate for a weather rule
findings.market: All 12 measured markets (no estimate yet for Mexico City)
findings.evidence: Rain effect on orders (95% range): Berlin +33.4% [30.3, 36.5], London +31.5% [28.9, 34.2], Paris +31.3% [28.6, 34.1], Amsterdam +18.1% [15.1, 21.1], Miami +16.8% [9.6, 24.3], Madrid +16.0% [12.5, 19.6], São Paulo +15.1% [9.9, 20.5], Milan +14.8%, New York +14.2%, Barcelona +14.0%, Lisbon +12.2% [8.3, 16.1]. Sample: 434 days per market (300 for São Paulo, 230 for Miami). Holiday effect is also positive: Miami +19.2%, Paris +18.5%, Madrid +12.7%. Heat lowers sales (Amsterdam -22.7% per 8°C). Next-14-day forecast uplift: Paris +9.9% / €39,729, São Paulo +10.2% / €39,558, London +5.4% / €26,320, Madrid +8.0% / €19,916, Barcelona +7.0% / €16,385. Extra return per extra euro of ad spend (marginal ROAS): São Paulo 3.81, London 3.01, Paris 2.60.

findings.title: Gifts: small positive rain effect, only significant in some markets; Beauty mostly zero
findings.evidence: Gifts rain effect +3.6% to +5.4%, range above zero in Madrid (+5.4 [1.7, 9.1]), Barcelona, Paris, London, Milan, Berlin, Amsterdam and New York. The range includes zero in Lisbon, São Paulo and Miami. Beauty is significant only in Paris (+4.2 [2.2, 6.3]), Amsterdam (+4.2 [1.7, 6.7]) and London (+3.0 [1.0, 5.0]); elsewhere the range spans zero. Gifts forecast uplift for the next 14 days is only 0.9–3.7% (largest: São Paulo, €11,179), so not worth a weather rule. Gifts responds to holidays instead: Paris +17.9%, London +15.3%, Milan +14.4%, Madrid +14.1%. Beauty mostly dips on holidays (Madrid -6.1%, São Paulo -6.7%).

findings.title: Fashion drops: rain reliably lowers sales – exclude it from any rain-boost rule
findings.evidence: Rain effect is negative everywhere: -2.5% (Amsterdam) to -6.7% (Barcelona, Milan); Paris -5.3% [-7.3, -3.3], London -5.4% [-7.4, -3.5]. São Paulo is the exception (-3.0, range [-8.2, 2.4] spans zero). Search interest falls seasonally from October to November (last year London -16%: 668,382 vs 796,303 searches).

findings.title: November seasonality and holidays: Gifts and US Home demand ramp sharply
findings.market: New York, London, Madrid, Berlin, Paris; holiday markets: FR, US, BR, MX, PT, ES
findings.evidence: Last year, November searches vs October (4 weeks each): New York Gifts +67% (821,667 vs 491,319), New York Home +55%, Madrid Gifts +35%, London Gifts +31%, Berlin Gifts +29%, Paris Gifts +23%. Public holidays in the next 4–5 weeks: 2 Nov (Brazil), 11 Nov (France + US), 15 and 20 Nov (Brazil), 16 Nov (Mexico), 26 Nov (US Thanksgiving), 1 Dec (Portugal), 6 Dec (Spain). Measured holiday effect: Paris Home +18.5%, Paris Gifts +17.9%, New York Home +6.5%, New York Gifts +5.3%, New York Fashion -6.6%.

findings.title: Madrid Beauty captures only 75% of its search demand – a long-standing reach gap, not a new failure
findings.evidence: Orders per 1,000 category searches: 16.17 vs 21.63 for peers; gap of 8,602 orders / €352,941 over 8 weeks (≈€176k/month as an upper bound). My own query shows the same capture rate last year (14.62 vs 14.61 now). Note: that query counted 23,031 orders against the tool's 25,503, probably a different date window. Revenue per day €16,877 vs €17,212 same period last year, so flat. Checkout-to-order rate 62.0% is within peer range (peer median 60.05), so this is not a conversion fault. Marginal ROAS 1.72 for the line overall (TikTok 4.44) is mid-table, below Home and Fashion drops in São Paulo, London and Paris, so this is not an obvious budget winner.

findings.title: Mexico City (new market) captures about half its potential and is ramping far slower than earlier launches
findings.evidence: Captured share 49–52% across all four lines; combined gap €374,445 over 8 weeks (Home €119,456, Fashion drops €105,182, Gifts €84,953, Beauty €64,854). The launch benchmark reports revenue per day of €2,535 at 8 weeks, vs Miami €36,690 and São Paulo €50,190 at the same age (6% of their median). That figure doesn't match the benchmark's own 28-day average of €10,416 (up from €3,255 the previous period), so treat it with caution. Not enough data yet to estimate weather effects.

proposed_actions.action: Turn on a rain rule for Home only, in the 11 markets with a significant measured effect. Over the next 14 days, prioritise Paris, São Paulo and London (best marginal ROAS: São Paulo TikTok 10.29, London creators 6.66, Paris creators 5.62).
proposed_actions.why: Rain lifts Home sales by 12–33%, with every 95% range above zero (434 days of data per established market). The forecast puts €39.7k, €39.6k and €26.3k of uplift in Paris, São Paulo and London. The demand model's holdout error is 6.4% (MAPE), with 82% of predictions within 10%.

proposed_actions.action: Keep Fashion drops, and Beauty outside Paris, London and Amsterdam, out of any rain rule. Consider trimming Fashion drops spend on forecast rainy days.
proposed_actions.why: Fashion drops is significantly negative in rain (about -5% to -7%). Beauty's rain effect is indistinguishable from zero in most markets.

proposed_actions.action: Shift budget toward Gifts in New York, London, Madrid, Berlin and Paris, and toward New York Home, through November. Set holiday flights around 11 Nov (France, US) and 26 Nov (US Thanksgiving).
proposed_actions.why: Last year's November search rose 23–67% for these lines, and Gifts sees a +14% to +18% holiday lift in Europe.

proposed_actions.action: Run a controlled spend test (+20%) on Madrid Beauty TikTok before any large reallocation.
proposed_actions.why: Low capture has persisted for a year and checkout is healthy. But the line's marginal ROAS (1.72) is middling, so the €353k gap over 8 weeks is an upper bound, not a guaranteed return.

proposed_actions.action: Pass the Mexico City launch ramp to the market lead and recheck the 8-week launch figure.
proposed_actions.why: Mexico City captures about 50% of its potential and sits far below earlier launches at the same age, but the benchmark's revenue figures don't agree with each other.

not_problems: Fashion drops falling on rainy days and in November is a measured, recurring pattern (rain -5% to -7%; November search was -16% in London last year), not a failure.
Madrid Beauty's low capture is not new: it was 14.62 orders per 1,000 searches last year vs 14.61 now, revenue is flat year on year, and checkout (62.0%) is within peer range.
Lines capturing over 100% of potential (Berlin Home 114%, Madrid Gifts 111%) are simply outperforming peers; nothing needs fixing.
Beauty and Fashion drops dipping on public holidays (e.g. Madrid Beauty -6.1%, New York Fashion -6.6%) is a normal holiday pattern.
The São Paulo heat effects for Fashion drops and Gifts (+172% and +181% per 8°C, from 300 days of data) look implausibly large; don't base spend rules on them.

input.summary: Two new problems are costing the most money. The first is a payment failure on Android checkout in Milan and Barcelona, at about €470k a month together. The second is late deliveries in London, at about €125k–197k a month. Next comes Madrid Home Edition 11, which was given 270 units against 8,334 for earlier editions and sold out on day 3, costing about €89k a month.

findings.title: Android checkout/payment failure (engineering)
findings.evidence: payment_problem comments: 22 of 227 (9.7%), up from 2.8%; 2.5% in other markets; p≈0. Milan Beauty: 8 of 56 (14.3%). Gist: 'payment would not go through', 'checkout page freezes when paying from phone'. Android checkout-to-order: 34.26% now vs 62.46% the previous 4 weeks, 61.42% last year and a 61.9–62.1% peer range. iOS is normal at 61.69%. Revenue per day: €44,274 now vs €52,012 the previous 4 weeks and €51,371 last year. NPS: -17 now vs -1 before.

findings.title: Android checkout/payment failure (engineering), same pattern as Milan
findings.evidence: payment_problem comments: 19 of 229 (8.3%), up from 1.4%; 2.6% elsewhere; p≈0. Gist: 'card gave an error', 'payment failed several times from mobile', 'payment page kept freezing'. Android checkout-to-order: 35.24% vs 62.8% the previous 4 weeks and 62.01% last year. iOS is normal at 62.52%. Revenue per day: €52,453 vs €60,433 the previous 4 weeks and €59,925 last year (€7,980 a day).

findings.title: Deliveries a week late (logistics)
findings.line: all lines (Fashion drops 42%, Home 35%, Beauty 29%, Gifts 23%)

input.summary: The most I can firmly report from the reallocation plan is €136.8k/week (about €592k/month) of extra revenue at the same total spend. That figure covers only the 19 market-lines I could read (the tool output was cut off); €84.2k/week of it (about €365k/month) sits in 11 market-lines where the model fits well (R² 0.80–0.99: São Paulo, Miami Home, New York, London Home/Gifts). The plan breaks its own ±50% cap (+58% to +69% on tiktok/youtube/creators), so these gains are optimistic. Phase it in at ±25%, keep cutting google_brand and meta_retargeting (marginal ROAS 0.0–1.2), and deal with October overspend: Madrid €55.6k (121%) and Lisbon €18.2k (109%) over budget, with no paid-revenue gain to show for it.

findings.title: Channel reallocation at the same total spend: €136.8k/week shown, €84.2k/week where the model fits well
findings.evidence: reallocation_plan output was cut off after 19 of 44 market-lines. Those 19 add up to €136,824/week (about €592k/month). The other 25 are each below €5,314/week, so the full total is higher but I couldn't sum it. 11 market-lines have R² ≥0.80 (São Paulo Home 0.988, Fashion 0.983, Gifts 0.99, Beauty 0.987; Miami Home 0.99; New York Home 0.858, Fashion 0.805, Gifts 0.949, Beauty 0.844; London Home 0.812, Gifts 0.927); together they give €84,202/week (+4.1% to +5.0% revenue each). Weak fits: Madrid Beauty 0.402, Paris Beauty 0.539, Paris Fashion 0.576, London Fashion 0.595, London Beauty 0.596, Madrid Fashion 0.611, Berlin Home 0.646 — treat these gains as directional only. The tools give no holdout error. The plan pushes increases to +58% to +69%, past the stated ±50% cap. That is outside the spend range the model has seen, so the gain is likely overstated. Gross profit cannot be calculated because the tools give no margin data.

You need to approve three low-risk rain rules, each adding 25% on rainy days: #8 Paris Home, #9 São Paulo Home and #10 London Home. Expect a Madrid Home spend cut (#3) and a possible portfolio-wide channel rebalance (#5) still waiting on approval.

output.summary: The two biggest problems are an Android checkout break in Barcelona and Milan since 14 Oct, worth about €700k/month in lost revenue together, and a Madrid Home stockout since 21 Oct, worth about €310k/month, with ads still running. Smaller items: London's email and SMS revenue has fallen, Lisbon spent more for no extra revenue, and Mexico City is far behind earlier launches. findings.title: Android checkout-to-order fell from about 62% to about 22% starting 14 Oct
findings.line: all lines (Home, Fashion drops, Beauty, Gifts all fell 62→54% overall)
findings.evidence: Android checkout-to-order went from 65.5% (550 checkouts) on 13 Oct to 21.5% (502 checkouts) on 14 Oct. It has stayed at 20–23% every day since. Weeks 3–4: 1,592 orders from 7,136 checkouts, against 62.8% in the prior 4 weeks (9,094 orders from 14,480 checkouts). Peer Android rate is 61.91–62.11% (last year 62.01%). iOS (62.9%) and desktop (60.6%) are unchanged, and order value is flat at €59.5. All of Barcelona's 28-day checkout-to-order is 54.0%, against a peer range of 61.96–61.97%. No significance test was run; the gap is about 40 points on roughly 3,500 checkouts a week.

findings.title: Same Android checkout break, starting the same day (14 Oct)
findings.evidence: Android checkout-to-order went from 58.4% (385 checkouts) on 13 Oct to 20.1% (442 checkouts) on 14 Oct. Weeks 3–4: 1,417 orders from 6,399 checkouts (about 22%), against 62.5% before (7,670 from 12,280). Peer range is 61.91–62.11%. iOS and desktop are normal at 61.6% and 63.1%. This one break explains all of Milan's other outliers: revenue/day €44.3k against a peer range of €52.5–56.0k (last year €51.4k), MER 5.44 against 6.33–6.66, and CPA €25.15 against €19.81–21.41.

findings.title: Home Edition 11 sold out on day 3 because it was stocked at 270 units instead of 8,334; ads kept running
findings.evidence: MAD-HOM-E10 (Edition 11) went on sale 19 Oct with capacity 270. Every other Madrid Home edition has 8,334, and it is the only product under 2,000 units. It was marked sold out on 21 Oct. Daily Home revenue fell from an average of €21.9k (12–21 Oct) to €11.6k (22 Oct–1 Nov), and sessions halved (about 9,400 to about 4,800 a day). Ad spend over those 11 sold-out days was still €29,057. Over 28 days, Madrid Home revenue was €497.9k against €562.4k before, and ROAS fell from 8.46 to 6.75.

findings.title: London's email and SMS revenue fell about 31%, which pulled repeat share below peers
findings.evidence: Repeat share is 8.87%, against 12.17% in the prior period, 12.77% last year and a peer range of 12.66–12.69%. Email sessions were about 21k a week until mid-September, then 17.3k in the week of 28 Sep and about 13–14k a week since. Email orders went from about 1,290 to about 830 a week, and SMS orders from about 450 to about 290 a week. Combined email and SMS revenue was €266.9k over 28 days, against €388.6k before. Other London channels are flat.

findings.title: Lisbon spent about 10% more with no extra revenue: MER and organic share are below peers
findings.line: all lines (spend rose on Beauty, Gifts and Home)
findings.evidence: MER is 4.82, against 5.58 in the prior period, 5.64 last year and a peer range of 5.44–6.33. Ad spend was €198.0k, against €179.7k in the prior period, while revenue was €953.8k against €1,002.5k. Paid share is 50.9% against a peer range of 43.8–44.1%; organic share is 37.2% against 44.34–44.35%. Revenue per search is in line with peers (Gifts 1.51, Home 1.52), so demand capture is fine and the problem is the extra spend.

findings.title: Mexico City launch is far behind earlier launches at the same age
findings.evidence: The market launched 6 Sep and is 8 weeks old. The benchmark tool puts revenue/day now at €2,535, against Miami at €36,690 and São Paulo at €50,190 at the same age (6% of their median). CPA is €38.87 against a peer range of €17.49–19.44 (down from €56.74). Revenue per search is 0.44 for Beauty, 0.64 for Fashion drops, 0.75 for Gifts and 0.82 for Home, against peers at about 0.75–1.5. Caveat: the same tool reports 28-day revenue/day as €10.4k, so the launch figure needs checking.

findings.title: Beauty captures much less of its search demand than peers, but this is long-standing
findings.evidence: Revenue per search is 0.62 (788,676 searches over 28 days), against about 0.72–0.86 in other Beauty markets (median about 0.79). It was 0.61 in the same period last year. Madrid's search volume is higher than Paris's with about half the population, so the search index may be inflated. Revenue/day is €17.6k, the same as last year (€17.7k) and above peers (€9.8–10.5k). The euro figure is the upper bound if Madrid reached the peer capture rate.

proposed_actions.action: Take Lisbon spend back to the previous level (about €180k per 4 weeks).

proposed_actions.action: Confirm Mexico City's launch revenue figures, then review CAC and the channel mix before scaling.

not_problems: New York revenue/day fell 24% against the prior 4 weeks (€96.3k vs €126.4k), but it matches last year (€99.0k). Search interest fell about 20% over the same time and revenue per search is flat (e.g. Home 1.40 vs 1.45). CPA is €21.54, against €22.28 last year. This is seasonal.

Milan's revenue, MER and CPA outliers are all caused by the Android checkout break, not by marketing.
iOS and desktop checkout-to-order are within the normal range in every market (the scans flagged nothing).
Madrid Beauty revenue is normal against last year and above peers; only its demand-capture ratio is low, and it was just as low last year.

Paris, São Paulo and London Home are the best places for a rain rule over the next 14 days, worth about €40k, €40k and €26k of forecast uplift; Fashion drops reliably loses sales in rain. The biggest uncaptured demand is Madrid Beauty (75% of potential, about €353k over 8 weeks). It is a long-standing reach gap, not a new failure, and November's seasonal and holiday demand (gift searches ramp, US Thanksgiving, French/US holiday on 11 Nov) argues for moving spend toward Gifts and Home, not Fashion drops.

findings.title: Home: strong, significant rain effect everywhere – the main candidate for a weather rule
findings.market: All 12 measured markets (no estimate yet for Mexico City)
findings.evidence: Rain effect on orders (95% range): Berlin +33.4% [30.3, 36.5], London +31.5% [28.9, 34.2], Paris +31.3% [28.6, 34.1], Amsterdam +18.1% [15.1, 21.1], Miami +16.8% [9.6, 24.3], Madrid +16.0% [12.5, 19.6], São Paulo +15.1% [9.9, 20.5], Milan +14.8%, New York +14.2%, Barcelona +14.0%, Lisbon +12.2% [8.3, 16.1]. Sample: 434 days per market (300 for São Paulo, 230 for Miami). Holiday effect is also positive: Miami +19.2%, Paris +18.5%, Madrid +12.7%. Heat lowers sales (Amsterdam -22.7% per 8°C). Next-14-day forecast uplift: Paris +9.9% / €39,729, São Paulo +10.2% / €39,558, London +5.4% / €26,320, Madrid +8.0% / €19,916, Barcelona +7.0% / €16,385. Extra return per extra euro of ad spend (marginal ROAS): São Paulo 3.81, London 3.01, Paris 2.60.

findings.title: Gifts: small positive rain effect, only significant in some markets; Beauty mostly zero
findings.evidence: Gifts rain effect +3.6% to +5.4%, range above zero in Madrid (+5.4 [1.7, 9.1]), Barcelona, Paris, London, Milan, Berlin, Amsterdam and New York. The range includes zero in Lisbon, São Paulo and Miami. Beauty is significant only in Paris (+4.2 [2.2, 6.3]), Amsterdam (+4.2 [1.7, 6.7]) and London (+3.0 [1.0, 5.0]); elsewhere the range spans zero. Gifts forecast uplift for the next 14 days is only 0.9–3.7% (largest: São Paulo, €11,179), so not worth a weather rule. Gifts responds to holidays instead: Paris +17.9%, London +15.3%, Milan +14.4%, Madrid +14.1%. Beauty mostly dips on holidays (Madrid -6.1%, São Paulo -6.7%).

findings.title: Fashion drops: rain reliably lowers sales – exclude it from any rain-boost rule
findings.evidence: Rain effect is negative everywhere: -2.5% (Amsterdam) to -6.7% (Barcelona, Milan); Paris -5.3% [-7.3, -3.3], London -5.4% [-7.4, -3.5]. São Paulo is the exception (-3.0, range [-8.2, 2.4] spans zero). Search interest falls seasonally from October to November (last year London -16%: 668,382 vs 796,303 searches).

findings.title: November seasonality and holidays: Gifts and US Home demand ramp sharply
findings.market: New York, London, Madrid, Berlin, Paris; holiday markets: FR, US, BR, MX, PT, ES
findings.evidence: Last year, November searches vs October (4 weeks each): New York Gifts +67% (821,667 vs 491,319), New York Home +55%, Madrid Gifts +35%, London Gifts +31%, Berlin Gifts +29%, Paris Gifts +23%. Public holidays in the next 4–5 weeks: 2 Nov (Brazil), 11 Nov (France + US), 15 and 20 Nov (Brazil), 16 Nov (Mexico), 26 Nov (US Thanksgiving), 1 Dec (Portugal), 6 Dec (Spain). Measured holiday effect: Paris Home +18.5%, Paris Gifts +17.9%, New York Home +6.5%, New York Gifts +5.3%, New York Fashion -6.6%.

findings.title: Madrid Beauty captures only 75% of its search demand – a long-standing reach gap, not a new failure
findings.evidence: Orders per 1,000 category searches: 16.17 vs 21.63 for peers; gap of 8,602 orders / €352,941 over 8 weeks (≈€176k/month as an upper bound). My own query shows the same capture rate last year (14.62 vs 14.61 now). Note: that query counted 23,031 orders against the tool's 25,503, probably a different date window. Revenue per day €16,877 vs €17,212 same period last year, so flat. Checkout-to-order rate 62.0% is within peer range (peer median 60.05), so this is not a conversion fault. Marginal ROAS 1.72 for the line overall (TikTok 4.44) is mid-table, below Home and Fashion drops in São Paulo, London and Paris, so this is not an obvious budget winner.

findings.title: Mexico City (new market) captures about half its potential and is ramping far slower than earlier launches
findings.evidence: Captured share 49–52% across all four lines; combined gap €374,445 over 8 weeks (Home €119,456, Fashion drops €105,182, Gifts €84,953, Beauty €64,854). The launch benchmark reports revenue per day of €2,535 at 8 weeks, vs Miami €36,690 and São Paulo €50,190 at the same age (6% of their median). That figure doesn't match the benchmark's own 28-day average of €10,416 (up from €3,255 the previous period), so treat it with caution. Not enough data yet to estimate weather effects.

proposed_actions.action: Turn on a rain rule for Home only, in the 11 markets with a significant measured effect. Over the next 14 days, prioritise Paris, São Paulo and London (best marginal ROAS: São Paulo TikTok 10.29, London creators 6.66, Paris creators 5.62).
proposed_actions.why: Rain lifts Home sales by 12–33%, with every 95% range above zero (434 days of data per established market). The forecast puts €39.7k, €39.6k and €26.3k of uplift in Paris, São Paulo and London. The demand model's holdout error is 6.4% (MAPE), with 82% of predictions within 10%.

proposed_actions.action: Keep Fashion drops, and Beauty outside Paris, London and Amsterdam, out of any rain rule. Consider trimming Fashion drops spend on forecast rainy days.
proposed_actions.why: Fashion drops is significantly negative in rain (about -5% to -7%). Beauty's rain effect is indistinguishable from zero in most markets.

proposed_actions.action: Shift budget toward Gifts in New York, London, Madrid, Berlin and Paris, and toward New York Home, through November. Set holiday flights around 11 Nov (France, US) and 26 Nov (US Thanksgiving).
proposed_actions.why: Last year's November search rose 23–67% for these lines, and Gifts sees a +14% to +18% holiday lift in Europe.

proposed_actions.action: Run a controlled spend test (+20%) on Madrid Beauty TikTok before any large reallocation.
proposed_actions.why: Low capture has persisted for a year and checkout is healthy. But the line's marginal ROAS (1.72) is middling, so the €353k gap over 8 weeks is an upper bound, not a guaranteed return.

proposed_actions.action: Pass the Mexico City launch ramp to the market lead and recheck the 8-week launch figure.
proposed_actions.why: Mexico City captures about 50% of its potential and sits far below earlier launches at the same age, but the benchmark's revenue figures don't agree with each other.

not_problems: Fashion drops falling on rainy days and in November is a measured, recurring pattern (rain -5% to -7%; November search was -16% in London last year), not a failure.
Madrid Beauty's low capture is not new: it was 14.62 orders per 1,000 searches last year vs 14.61 now, revenue is flat year on year, and checkout (62.0%) is within peer range.
Lines capturing over 100% of potential (Berlin Home 114%, Madrid Gifts 111%) are simply outperforming peers; nothing needs fixing.
Beauty and Fashion drops dipping on public holidays (e.g. Madrid Beauty -6.1%, New York Fashion -6.6%) is a normal holiday pattern.
The São Paulo heat effects for Fashion drops and Gifts (+172% and +181% per 8°C, from 300 days of data) look implausibly large; don't base spend rules on them.

output.summary: Two new problems are costing the most money. The first is a payment failure on Android checkout in Milan and Barcelona, at about €470k a month together. The second is late deliveries in London, at about €125k–197k a month. Next comes Madrid Home Edition 11, which was given 270 units against 8,334 for earlier editions and sold out on day 3, costing about €89k a month.

findings.title: Android checkout/payment failure (engineering)
findings.evidence: payment_problem comments: 22 of 227 (9.7%), up from 2.8%; 2.5% in other markets; p≈0. Milan Beauty: 8 of 56 (14.3%). Gist: 'payment would not go through', 'checkout page freezes when paying from phone'. Android checkout-to-order: 34.26% now vs 62.46% the previous 4 weeks, 61.42% last year and a 61.9–62.1% peer range. iOS is normal at 61.69%. Revenue per day: €44,274 now vs €52,012 the previous 4 weeks and €51,371 last year. NPS: -17 now vs -1 before.

findings.title: Android checkout/payment failure (engineering), same pattern as Milan
findings.evidence: payment_problem comments: 19 of 229 (8.3%), up from 1.4%; 2.6% elsewhere; p≈0. Gist: 'card gave an error', 'payment failed several times from mobile', 'payment page kept freezing'. Android checkout-to-order: 35.24% vs 62.8% the previous 4 weeks and 62.01% last year. iOS is normal at 62.52%. Revenue per day: €52,453 vs €60,433 the previous 4 weeks and €59,925 last year (€7,980 a day).

findings.title: Deliveries a week late (logistics)
findings.line: all lines (Fashion drops 42%, Home 35%, Beauty 29%, Gifts 23%)
findings.evidence: delivery_late comments: 70 of 219 (32.0%) vs 4.9% before and 5.4% elsewhere; p≈0. Fashion drops: 22 of 52. Gist: 'promised Friday, arrived the following Thursday'; 'tracking stalled'. NPS: -35 now vs -7 before. Repeat-customer share: 8.87% vs 12.17% the previous 4 weeks, 12.77% last year and a 12.66–12.69% peer range. Revenue per day: €107,431 vs €113,990 the previous 4 weeks and €111,614 last year. The €125k figure is the gap to last year; the gap to the previous 4 weeks is about €197k.

findings.title: Limited edition given too little stock and sold out on day 3 (ops/merchandising)
findings.evidence: Edition 11 launched 2026-10-19 with 270 units of stock; Editions 4–10 each had 8,334. Stockout logged 2026-10-21. Units per day fell from 99.7 (days 1–3) to 54.6 (days 4–14). Earlier editions sold about 88–104 a day over days 4–14. The gap is about 40 units a day at €74. sold_out is the top theme for Madrid Home since launch (6 comments): 'out of stock when they tried to buy'. The edition runs until 2026-11-29.

findings.title: Website hard to navigate (product), but no revenue impact yet
findings.evidence: website_ux comments: 49 of 235 (20.9%) vs 6.5% before and 4.1% elsewhere. Gifts: 17 of 58 (29.3%). Gist: 'website is confusing to navigate'. Checkout-to-order is flat: 61.74% vs 61.93% the previous 4 weeks and 62.09% last year. Gifts revenue is €8,368 a day vs €8,171 the previous 4 weeks. Lisbon revenue is 10% below last year, but this theme cannot be shown to explain it.

findings.title: Low brand awareness/trust in a new market (creative)
findings.evidence: trust_brand comments: 29 of 223 (13.0%) vs 2.5% elsewhere, already falling from 15.1%. Gist: 'never heard of the brand, is it trustworthy?'. At week 8 after launch, the latest revenue per day is €2,535: 6% of what earlier launches (Miami, São Paulo) made at the same age. NPS is improving: +1 now vs -32 before.

proposed_actions.action: Engineering: fix the Android payment step in Milan and Barcelona now. Check the payment provider and its Android setup there, compare with Madrid and Berlin, and look at what was released around the start of October.
proposed_actions.why: Android checkout-to-order fell from ~62% to ~35% in both markets while iOS stayed normal. Together that is about €470k a month.

proposed_actions.action: Logistics: escalate with the London carrier. Fix stalled tracking, update the promised delivery dates on the site, and proactively contact late orders, with credit for repeat buyers.
proposed_actions.why: 32% of London comments are about week-late deliveries, NPS fell from -7 to -35, and the repeat-customer share is down about a third.

proposed_actions.action: Ops: restock or reallocate Madrid Home Edition 11 before it ends on 2026-11-29. Write a stock-planning rule so limited editions are not given 270 units against the 8,334 of earlier ones.
proposed_actions.why: Sales halved after the day-3 stockout, costing about €3k a day.

proposed_actions.action: Product: run a navigation/usability review of Lisbon's Gifts and Beauty pages. Watch conversion, but don't put this ahead of the items above.
proposed_actions.why: The complaint is new and frequent, but conversion and Gifts revenue have not dropped yet.

proposed_actions.action: Creative: add trust signals to Mexico City ads and site (reviews, guarantees, social proof).
proposed_actions.why: Unfamiliarity with the brand is the theme that stands out most there, and the launch is far behind earlier launches at the same age.

not_problems: Price/value complaints are the largest complaint theme but are falling: 288 in the last 4 weeks vs 347 before. Positive product and service comments are stable (554/313 vs 596/309).
Sizing, returns, customer service, sold-out (outside Madrid Home) and ad-fatigue comments are flat or down across markets and nothing stands out.
Madrid Beauty 'wants more range' is 15.6% of comments but not new (14.6% before). It is a range request, not a fault.
Lisbon's checkout is normal at 61.7%, in line with last year. The website complaints there have not yet hurt sales.
Mexico City's trust problem is normal for a new market and is improving (theme share 15.1%→13.0%, NPS -32→+1).
Amsterdam, São Paulo and Miami NPS rose (-23→-2, -10→+4, -12→-5). There is no new problem there.

output.summary: The most I can firmly report from the reallocation plan is €136.8k/week (about €592k/month) of extra revenue at the same total spend. That figure covers only the 19 market-lines I could read (the tool output was cut off); €84.2k/week of it (about €365k/month) sits in 11 market-lines where the model fits well (R² 0.80–0.99: São Paulo, Miami Home, New York, London Home/Gifts). The plan breaks its own ±50% cap (+58% to +69% on tiktok/youtube/creators), so these gains are optimistic. Phase it in at ±25%, keep cutting google_brand and meta_retargeting (marginal ROAS 0.0–1.2), and deal with October overspend: Madrid €55.6k (121%) and Lisbon €18.2k (109%) over budget, with no paid-revenue gain to show for it.

findings.title: Channel reallocation at the same total spend: €136.8k/week shown, €84.2k/week where the model fits well
findings.evidence: reallocation_plan output was cut off after 19 of 44 market-lines. Those 19 add up to €136,824/week (about €592k/month). The other 25 are each below €5,314/week, so the full total is higher but I couldn't sum it. 11 market-lines have R² ≥0.80 (São Paulo Home 0.988, Fashion 0.983, Gifts 0.99, Beauty 0.987; Miami Home 0.99; New York Home 0.858, Fashion 0.805, Gifts 0.949, Beauty 0.844; London Home 0.812, Gifts 0.927); together they give €84,202/week (+4.1% to +5.0% revenue each). Weak fits: Madrid Beauty 0.402, Paris Beauty 0.539, Paris Fashion 0.576, London Fashion 0.595, London Beauty 0.596, Madrid Fashion 0.611, Berlin Home 0.646 — treat these gains as directional only. The tools give no holdout error. The plan pushes increases to +58% to +69%, past the stated ±50% cap. That is outside the spend range the model has seen, so the gain is likely overstated. Gross profit cannot be calculated because the tools give no margin data.

findings.title: Ad fatigue: BER-BTY-META-PROSPECTING
findings.evidence: Frequency rose from 2.5 to 5.1 (last 7 days) and CTR fell from 1.11% to 0.70%. CPA €35.2 vs €25 target; €14.4k spend over 28 days. It is the only ad with frequency above 3 or a CTR drop of more than 20%.

findings.title: Ads with CPA far above the €25 target (affiliates and meta_retargeting)
findings.evidence: Last 28 days, CPA / ROAS / CPA a year ago: NYC-FSH-AFFILIATES €73.7 / 0.79 / €69.4; BCN-FSH-AFFILIATES €73.2 / 0.79 / €44.5; LIS-GFT-META-RETARGETING €73.2 / 0.90 / €76.5; LIS-HOM-META-RETARGETING €69.7 / 1.07 / €54.9; NYC-GFT-AFFILIATES €68.7 / 0.96 / €47.5; MAD-HOM-AFFILIATES €66.1; MIL-HOM-AFFILIATES €63.6; AMS-GFT-META-RETARGETING €61.8; AMS-FSH-META-RETARGETING €58.6; MIL-FSH-GOOGLE-GENERIC €57.7 (€11.9k spend, ROAS 0.99, €43.3 a year ago). Many were similar last year, so part of this is structural. The €25 target is hard to hit on last-click for these channels.

proposed_actions.action: In the 11 market-lines with R² ≥0.80, move spend from google_brand (−25%) and meta_retargeting (−25%) into tiktok, youtube and creators (+25% each), keeping each market-line's total the same. Run a geo holdout before going further toward the plan's split.
proposed_actions.why: The full plan is worth €84.2k/week in these market-lines, but it relies on +58% to +69% increases outside the spend range the model has seen. A ±25% step stays closer to tested spend levels. Expect less than the full gain; I haven't modelled the exact amount.

proposed_actions.action: In weak-fit market-lines (R² <0.65: Madrid Beauty and Fashion, Paris Beauty and Fashion, London Fashion and Beauty, Berlin Home), make only small cuts to google_brand and run lift tests before scaling up.
proposed_actions.why: Local and pooled elasticities disagree badly (Madrid Beauty meta_prospecting 0.068 vs 0.965 pooled), so the estimates could be off by a factor of several.

proposed_actions.action: Bring Madrid and Lisbon back to budget (−€55.6k and −€18.2k a month), starting with meta_retargeting and google_brand. Shift Beauty budget in Lisbon, Amsterdam and Milan (blended marginal ROAS 0.82–1.11) toward São Paulo, London Home and Miami Home (2.6–3.8).
proposed_actions.why: The extra spend in October brought no paid-revenue gain, and the money earns 2–4x more at the margin elsewhere.

proposed_actions.action: Refresh the creative on BER-BTY-META-PROSPECTING or cap its frequency. Review bids or cut NYC-FSH-AFFILIATES, BCN-FSH-AFFILIATES, NYC-GFT-AFFILIATES, LIS-GFT- and LIS-HOM-META-RETARGETING, and MIL-FSH-GOOGLE-GENERIC.
proposed_actions.why: Frequency on the Berlin ad is 5.1 and its CTR fell 37%. The others have CPAs of €58–74 and last-click ROAS below 1.1.

proposed_actions.action: Plan budgets on first-party and model figures rather than platform ROAS.
proposed_actions.why: Platforms over-claim revenue by 1.1–2.1x (meta_retargeting 3.49 vs 1.64, youtube 5.74 vs 2.92).

not_problems: Mexico City spent only 22.3% of its October budget and is projected at 30.3% for November. It launched on 2026-09-07 and is still ramping: daily spend went from €47 to €2,722 and daily revenue reached €5,367. Days where individual MEX ads show clicks but zero sessions are low-volume launch noise; total sessions grew to 2,034 a day. I found no persistent broken links.
Every google_brand ad records about 18% CTR, but sessions are only about 15–20% of clicks. The pattern is identical across all markets, so it's how clicks are counted, not broken links.
Retargeting ads with a single day of 11 sessions (LIS, BCN, AMS, MAD) were one-day blips, not lasting outages.

Organic revenue in New York (−24% vs the prior 28 days), Barcelona and Milan dropped in step with paid revenue while spend stayed flat; New York is only −2.5% vs last year, which suggests a seasonal or demand dip. Search elasticity in the model is about 0.96, so demand drives revenue more than ads do.
November pacing projections of 91–106% are based on 1 day (3.3% of the month), which is too early to call overspend or underspend.

WITH a AS (SELECT ad_id, market, line, platform, SUM(spend) sp, SUM(link_clicks) cl, SUM(impressions) im, AVG(frequency) fq,
 SUM(CASE WHEN day>'2026-10-18' THEN link_clicks END)*1.0/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN day>'2026-10-18' THEN impressions END),0) ctr_recent,
 SUM(CASE WHEN day<='2026-10-18' THEN link_clicks END)*1.0/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN day<='2026-10-18' THEN impressions END),0) ctr_prior,
 AVG(CASE WHEN day>'2026-10-25' THEN frequency END) fq_recent
 FROM ad_daily WHERE day>'2026-10-04' GROUP BY ad_id),
s AS (SELECT ad_id, SUM(sessions) se, SUM(orders) o, SUM(revenue) r FROM sales_daily WHERE day>'2026-10-04' AND ad_id<>'' GROUP BY ad_id)
SELECT a.ad_id, market, line, platform, ROUND(sp) sp, cl, s.se, s.o, ROUND(sp/NULLIF(s.o,0),1) cpa, ROUND(fq_recent,1) fq7, ROUND(ctr_prior*100,2) ctr_p, ROUND(ctr_recent*100,2) ctr_r
FROM a LEFT JOIN s USING(ad_id)
WHERE (s.se IS NULL OR s.se < 0.2*cl) OR fq_recent>5 OR ctr_recent<0.6*ctr_prior OR sp/NULLIF(s.o,0) > 80 OR s.o IS NULL OR s.o=0
ORDER BY sp DESC LIMIT 60

WITH a AS (SELECT day, ad_id, market, line, spend, link_clicks FROM ad_daily WHERE day>'2026-10-11'),
s AS (SELECT day, ad_id, SUM(sessions) se, SUM(orders) o FROM sales_daily WHERE day>'2026-10-11' AND ad_id<>'' GROUP BY day, ad_id)
SELECT a.ad_id, a.market, a.line, MIN(a.day) first_zero, COUNT(*) days, ROUND(SUM(a.spend)) spend, SUM(a.link_clicks) clicks, SUM(COALESCE(s.se,0)) sessions, SUM(COALESCE(s.o,0)) orders
FROM a LEFT JOIN s ON s.day=a.day AND s.ad_id=a.ad_id
WHERE a.link_clicks>=20 AND COALESCE(s.se,0) < 0.05*a.link_clicks
GROUP BY a.ad_id ORDER BY spend DESC LIMIT 30
